content.text: {"schema":"zcl.command_spec.v1","path":"fleet.machines","summary":"List the computers admitted to this fleet","availability":"ready","semantics":"Verified roster rows, oldest first, each split into `verified` (what the operator signature attests: name, box public key, relay port, enrolment time) and `self_reported` (what the box said about its own hardware, OS and toolchain — signed by that box, measured by nobody). The two are never merged. The NAME leads every row and does not change with the box's onion address, Noise fingerprint or ZID. Rows this operator key did not seal are counted in `unverifiable` and never rendered, and they do not consume a page slot. Optional `offset` and `limit` select one page of verified rows; `limit` is at least 1 and is capped at the render maximum, so a hand-grown roster past that cap is reached by a later offset rather than a larger reply. `total` counts every verified row, `returned` is this page, `truncated` means a later page exists, and `next_offset` is -1 on the last page. Absent keys read the first page. Reads no node: when the CLI was given --datadir it opens that node.db READ-ONLY, never creating it, and reports `operator_anchor` — whether this fleet's operator key is an active ZID anchor (state active, rotated, revoked, not_anchored, unchecked or unreadable). That state is reported, never enforced: an enrolment made before the key was anchored still lists.","registry_digest":"sha256:3b6d9157a865649edd33490e0d159e140111a8519644c1f68bad507f72cd81ac","input_schema":{"id":"zcl.fleet_machines_input.v1","allowed_keys":["offset","limit"],"positional_keys":[]},"output_schema":"zcl.fleet.machines.v1","policy":{"layer":"app","effect":"read","risk":"read","scope":"local","authority":"owner","mode":"sync","latency":"fast","cost":"low","confirmation":"none","deterministic":false,"idempotent":true,"display_only":false,"prose":false,"allowed_lanes":1,"required_capabilities":0,"budget_bytes":65536,"budget_ms":250,"observed_p99_us":0,"observed_samples":0},"example":"z23 fleet machines --input='{\"offset\":0,\"limit\":64}'"}
